_description: Task13 DRIFT field, FINE transcription -- the 0.1mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume, for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch, 15cm drift. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.55mm far-field grid. PHASE 4 RETARGET: only the DEPTH and the VOLTAGE moved in this file. Every geometry value is unchanged, because at 0.1mm every true design length is already an exact whole number of cells -- pixelSize 3.5 -> 35 cells, pixelGap 0.9 -> 9, chamfer_r 0.7 -> 7 (via int(round()) in the generator; 0.7/0.1 is 6.999999999999999 in binary float, so the rounding is load-bearing). NOTHING IS SNAPPED HERE, which is the opposite of the coarse file; here the values ARE the design values. THE BULK FIELD IS NOW 50.0 V/mm, NOT 56.0 -- READ THIS BEFORE 'RESTORING' ANYTHING. CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition) = -50.0 * (149.55 - 9.9) = -6982.5 V. This is a DELIBERATE change of the design field, not a rescaling that preserves it. The previous -3878 V existed specifically to hold 56.0 V/mm across the 8cm geometry. That choice has been GIVEN UP. Do not 'fix' this back to 56.0 V/mm: drift velocities and induced currents from this geometry are NOT comparable to the 8cm results, because velo derives mobility from E through a nonlinear LAr parameterisation, so a 10.7% lower field is not a 10.7% slower drift. The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose. The SAME voltage is applied on the coarse and the fine grid, deliberately: it is a boundary condition. 1.1mm IS THE SHARED PERIOD of the 0.1mm and 0.55mm grids, and every plane that must land on both is a whole multiple of it: pitch 4.4 = 44 fine / 8 coarse cells, pad plane 9.9 = 99 / 18, interface 29.7 = 297 / 54, cathode 149.6 = 1496 / 272. PITCH: 3.5 + 0.9 = 4.4mm = 44 fine cells and 8 coarse cells of 0.55mm. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise. PIXEL PLANE LOW EDGE 9.9 IS LOAD-BEARING: 9.9mm is 99 fine cells AND 18 coarse cells of 0.55mm, so the pad plane lands on a real node of BOTH grids. Moving it breaks that co-location. (The generator reads this key with int(), not int(round()) -- gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py:474 -- so never reason about it in decimal; 9.9/0.1 is exactly 99.0 and 9.9/0.55 exactly 18.0 in binary float, but neighbouring values are not so lucky.) DEPTH: driftZDepth 149.55 is the electron LAUNCH node, deliberately NOT rounded to 149.6. The cathode sits on the domain's last plane at ceil(149.55/0.55) = 272 coarse cells = 149.6mm, which is 1496 fine cells exactly, so both grids close on the same physical cathode; the launch node itself does not land on that grounded plane, which is the point. The fine z grid is 1497 nodes. THE PAD SURFACE THIS FILE DEFINES IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. padThickness 0.05 and FR4Thickness 0.1 each round to ONE cell here (n_pad is clamped to a 1-cell minimum because 0.05 is half a cell), so the generator derives pp_width = n_pad + n_fr4 - 1 = 1 and the pad TOP is at (99+1)*0.1 = 10.00mm. This fine config and the weighting field's fine config must AGREE on that surface, because both fields' near solves and ALL drift paths live on this 0.1mm grid. The coarse files only supply the far field beyond the 29.7mm interface, where the pad's discretisation no longer shapes the geometry, only the far amplitude. The coarse grid's own pad top is 10.45mm -- a 0.45mm disagreement that is expected and is NOT to be compensated for with different voltages. EXPECTATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT -- for Phase 4/Step 6: no far-field E_z has been solved for on this geometry. Every 'measured' figure from the 8cm transcription (55.885 V/mm on this grid, 55.996 coarse, the 0.199% spread, the 56.498/56.040 chord numbers, the index-115 grid-plane check) has been DELETED rather than carried over: different depth, different spacing, different field. Do not reinstate any of it, and do not write a new number here until it has been measured. The coarse/fine spread is EXPECTED to exceed 0.199% because the coarse pad-area snap worsened from +1.1% to -11.1%. pixelPlaneWidth 0.1 is INERT in this configuration: with enableInsulatorFR4 true and both thickness keys present, the generator derives pp_width and overwrites whatever this key says. SHIELD GRID OFF (GridHoleShape 'None'): inherited from the older with-grid task13 work, never intended for this WOGRID LArPix v2a geometry. GridPotential/PcbWidth/HoleRadius are inert and left in place. GridPotential does NOT enter the cathode calculation: the bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. TILE SIZE: Npixels 5, i.e. a 5x5 pad tile at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse for the weighting probe; the DRIFT field is one periodic tile, so Npixels does not size this file's domain.
